tldr: The mandate was NOT fully met. The session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200), so 0 of the 40+ required searches ran. WebFetch returned EGRESS_BLOCKED for mpay.cards, trustpilot, pintopay, bitrefill, reloadly, wanttopay, virtcardpay, redotpay and docs.stripe.com. No provider page, ToS, review page or API doc was seen first-hand. Overall confidence is low.

Everything in the deliverables comes from the repo's first-pass research (secondary), specialist 05/06 outputs, or is null + UNVERIFIED + verify_how. No Iran-eligibility ToS quote could be obtained, so every provider carries 'unknown_assume_ineligible_until_written_confirmation'. BaaS issuers and exchange-issued cards are marked 'ineligible_expected'.

mpay (secondary, low): issue USD 4.99, min load USD 25, monthly USD 0, networks TRC20/BEP20, top-up % unpublished (3.0% placeholder, band 0-5%). No public API or partner programme found, so all operations are panel/operator. Trustpilot is about 3/5 with fund-blocked complaints. The Dec-2025 USD 3M round is unverified.

Cost model: with the 3% placeholder, mpay overhead above face is USD 0.75/1.50/3.00/15.00 for top-ups of 25/50/100/500. New card + load is USD 5.74/6.49/7.99/19.99, i.e. 22.96%/12.98%/7.99%/4.00% of face. At tickets of USD 50 or less the fixed issue fee, not the percentage, decides profitability. Minimum new-card load for <=8% overhead is about USD 99.80.

Alternatives covered: 4 with reported fees (PintoPay, VirtCardPay, Wanttopay, AnyXPay), 6 with no data (uCards, Kripicard, PayX, MPChat, RedotPay, Cryptomus), 2 exchange cards, 5 voucher aggregators and 6 BaaS issuers. The supplier strategy has a three-gate rule: written eligibility reply, small live test, counsel-reviewed ToS snapshot. Float cap is <=5% of equity and <=3 days. A capability matrix mapped to ProviderCapabilities and a 40-query re-run plan are included.
data/providers.json validates OK (24 providers, 639 records, 487 UNVERIFIED). No git commit or push was done.

conflicts: mpay issue fee and min load are rated 'medium' in data/catalog.json and data/competitors.json but trace to one internal chain of secondary summaries. I rated them 'low' here until verified first-hand. Values are unchanged.
mpay top-up 3.0% (lead's model) vs 'unpublished' (first-pass text) is not a true conflict. It is stored as topup_pct_assumed (3.0) with topup_pct = null.

'No KYC' marketing vs the sanctions/counterparty-risk view: treated as compatible. No-KYC onboarding does not mean ToS permits Iran-resident customers, so eligibility is unknown and assumed ineligible.
The PintoPay (0.25 USD) and Wanttopay (0.30 USD) 'transaction' fees could be per spend or per load. I modelled them conservatively as per load.
Binance's stated policy blocks Iran users, while the AMLBot/Reuters relay reports large flows for an Iranian exchange. Policy governs eligibility, so I do not rely on enforcement gaps.
open_questions: Does mpay (or any alternative) accept Iran-resident business customers? Quote the ToS clause, snapshot it with a hash, get a written support reply and a counsel review.
What are mpay's real top-up %, fixed fee, FX %, decline fee, inactivity fee and refund-of-unused-balance rule? Fund a test account and read the fee table and statement.
What are mpay's legal entity, jurisdiction, licences and team, and is the Dec-2025 USD 3M round real? Check Whois, the ToS, a press release and Crunchbase.
What are mpay's per-card, daily and monthly limits, min deposit, credit time and confirmations? Check the in-account limits screen and a test deposit.
Does mpay have any private API, white-label or partner programme? Send a written enquiry to sales or support.

Run the 40-query re-run plan in section 9 of the doc (EN + FA) once the search budget is raised. It covers Trustpilot dates, Persian forums, the uCards/Kripicard/PayX/MPChat/RedotPay/Cryptomus fee data, the aggregator API/reseller terms and the BaaS eligibility wording.
Which card BIN/region and billing-address behaviour apply at each target merchant class? Issue a test card and run a USD 5 test per merchant class.
